conflicts.point: Whether algorithmic targeting systems reduce collateral error rates in operational deployments compared to biological human crews.

positions.stance: Algorithmic targeting systems process sensor data faster than human crews and reduce collateral error variances by eliminating combat fatigue.
Closed-source models lack empirical validation and routinely exhibit degraded accuracy under distribution shifts during live combat testing.

conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment software validation should follow civil aviation (FAA) multi-year testing standards or rapid iterative telemetry verification.

positions.stance: Enforcing multi-year civil aviation testing standards guarantees tactical obsolescence; safety must be established through runtime telemetry and probabilistic monitoring.
High-risk sectors require exhaustive pre-deployment empirical validation equivalent to civil aviation standards before operational use.

verdicts.conflict: Whether algorithmic targeting systems reduce collateral error rates in operational deployments compared to biological human crews.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position prevails because closed-source models lack public empirical validation and frequently encounter accuracy degradation during live distribution shifts. The accelerationist claim relies on theoretical speed metrics that remain shielded by proprietary restrictions rather than peer-reviewed operational data.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Independent and transparent testing data from live combat deployments demonstrating consistent error reduction across diverse operational environments would reverse this assessment.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment software validation should follow civil aviation (FAA) multi-year testing standards or rapid iterative telemetry verification.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist framework provides concrete validation mechanisms modeled on established high-risk safety regimes like civil aviation. The accelerationist reliance on runtime telemetry lacks comparable enforcement standards and fails to catch latent behavioral flaws prior to deployment.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that runtime probabilistic monitoring detects latent behavioral anomalies as reliably as exhaustive static code inspections would tip the balance.
